comparisons.D1_sigma_with_hard: for each irreversible cell, sign of the soft sigma against the sign of the partner index (and HELD handover index), beside the same soft term without a hard component (E2A)
comparisons.D2_one_way_mode: one-way flux share and its split by action and class; partner index of cells with sigma = 0 and one-way transitions
comparisons.D3_enabling_and_direction: strict enabling shares (matched dissolution) against irreversible flux, per cell
comparisons.D4_race: race committor from x- over strictly enabled instances against all instances and against the matched x with g present
comparisons.D5_scaffold: HELD versus FREE for each hard component (the source triangle as a witness)

controls_and_identities.I1_I2: as E2A: the square identity on intact squares, zero on disjoint squares
controls_and_identities.I6_hard_gradient_alone: adj_form prohibit alone (HAF-none), HELD and FREE: a gradient restriction; flux <= 1e-9 and no one-way transitions (forward and reverse rates vanish together within the class)
controls_and_identities.Z5_numerical: as E2A, plus the race committor converging (max change < 1e-14) before 20,000 iterations
controls_and_identities.separation_note: no expectation on the sign or size of any index, flux, enabling share or race probability

deliberate_omissions.HPF+PFws: path_form soft terms can never act under path_form prohibit (a witness forbids formation outright)
deliberate_omissions.n6_free_strong_grades_hard_dissolution: held out for a possible future confirmatory test (gt-e2a-reflection.md section 5)

estimands: every E2A channel plus one-way flux and the race committor, for each cell; D1-D5
numerical_policy: as E2A (gte2a numerical checks with round_id round-e2b), race committor by value iteration to max change < 1e-14, cap 20,000
open_questions_without_prediction: Is the one-way mode (hard path-form exclusion) oriented in the partner frame regardless of an added soft sigma of either sign, or does the soft sigma decide?
Does sigma predict the partner-index sign when a hard closure or adjacency exclusion is present?
What share of flux do one-way transitions carry, and is it formation or dissolution that cannot be reversed?
Do strictly enabled events win the race against restoration more often than other events, and more than from the matched state with the support present?
Does strict enabling ever come without any irreversibility apart from the hard-gradient controls?
How does the held source act as a witness under each hard component?

pre_freeze_exposure.e2a: all E2A results were read in full (they motivate E2B); the cited comparators are E2A cells
pre_freeze_exposure.e2b_cells: no E2B cell (hard component crossed with a soft term, or adj_form prohibit) was computed before freezing; plumbing tests use synthetic N=4 cells

question: Where admissibility rather than rate structures succession: when does strict enabling by dissolution come with direction, is the one-way mode oriented by its own rule, and does sigma still predict orientation under a hard component?
sampling: exact census of 18 declared cells at N=5, HELD and FREE
selection_rule: the three existing hard formation exclusions (path_form, close_form, adj_form prohibit) crossed with no soft term and the four weak path terms (path_dissolve weak_favour/weak_suppress, path_form weak_suppress/weak_favour); combinations run in E2A are cited, path_form soft terms are omitted under path_form prohibit

stop_conditions.amendment: cell or estimand changes stop the round
stop_conditions.round: all items or 3600 s; then stop

work_count.estimate_note: E2A N=5 cells took seconds; the race committor adds up to 90 value iterations of <= 1,024 states per cell: estimated under 2 minutes per cell
